> 「是法平等，无有高下，是名阿耨多罗三藐三菩提。以无我、无人、无众生、无寿者，修一切善法，即得阿耨多罗三藐三菩提。」

If one sentence in this sutra is to be written on a wall, it is the second sentence of section twenty-three.

以无我、无人、无众生、无寿者，修一切善法，即得阿耨多罗三藐三菩提.

With no mark of self, person, being, or lifespan — practise all good dharmas — and awakening is attained.

Two halves, and both are load-bearing. The first is the quality of the mind. The second is the action in the world. Drop either half and the sentence collapses into something the sutra is not saying.

## 是法平等，无有高下

Equality here is not "everything is equally good". The book is exact: 平等 means there is no dimension of higher and lower — not that the differences have been erased.

That matters because the difference is operational. Causes and effects differ sharply; kindness and cruelty are not the same; a clear mind and a confused one are not equivalent. What is absent is the *ranking* — the vertical axis on which one stands above another.

And then: this absence of a ranking is itself what is called awakening. Not "the highest" — 无高下.

Which is a strange and precise claim. Every other attainment is comparative by nature; this one cannot be, because the comparison is what it removes.

## 修一切善法 is not optional

The second half is an imperative: practise all good dharmas.

The book spends commentary defending this against its two distortions:

- The emptiness distortion: since all is empty, conduct is irrelevant. Refuted by the plain words 修一切善法 — the sutra commands the practice, not the theory of it.
- The merit distortion: since good dharmas produce good results, accumulate them. Refuted by 即非善法 — good dharmas have no own-nature either, so they cannot be banked.

The command and the cancellation are in the same breath, which is the only way either of them works.

## 即得 is not "one day"

Note the character 即 — immediately, right at that point.

Not: practise for aeons, and eventually attain. The sentence says that in the moment of practising good dharmas without the four marks, awakening is — not will be.

That is not a claim about speed. It is a statement about location: awakening is not downstream of the practice, produced by it. It is the practice's own texture, described from inside.

## The two failures, precisely

With the marks and without the practice: a person who has understood emptiness and does nothing. Serene, useless, and usually pleased with themselves.

With the practice and without the marks: a person who does enormous good and keeps the ledger. The book's phrase for this is 我相的精装版 — the self in a better suit. Everything looks right; the structure has not changed.

The section's formula is the only configuration in which neither failure occurs, and it is stated once, plainly, without ornament.

## The test

Take one good act available to you today. Not a large one — the kind you could actually do before evening.

Do it, and while doing it, check both halves. Is anything being asked for in return — gratitude, credit, the feeling of being good?

If something is being asked for, you are in the second failure. The act is still worth doing. But it is being done by someone, and that someone is what the first half of the sentence removes.
